definitions.explanation: a camera that uses a mirror mechanism to show the exact image that will be captured through the lens

examples.japanese: {一眼|いちがん}レフを{買|か}った。
{一眼|いちがん}レフは{初心者|しょしんしゃ}には{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: SLR cameras are difficult for beginners.

examples.japanese: プロの{写真家|しゃしんか}は{一眼|いちがん}レフを{使|つか}うことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Professional photographers often use SLR cameras.

notes:
{一眼|いちがん}レフ is the Japanese term for SLR (single-lens reflex) camera, a popular type among photography enthusiasts.

ETYMOLOGY:
- {一眼|いちがん} (single lens/eye)
- レフ (reflex, from German "Reflex")
- Full term: {一眼|いちがん}レフレックスカメラ

TYPES:
- {一眼|いちがん}レフ / SLR (traditional with mirror)
- ミラーレス{一眼|いちがん} (mirrorless) - newer technology
- デジタル{一眼|いちがん}レフ / DSLR (digital SLR)

FEATURES:
- {交換|こうかん}{式|しき}レンズ (interchangeable lenses)
- {光学|こうがく}ファインダー (optical viewfinder)
- Larger sensors than compact cameras

COMMON BRANDS IN JAPAN:
- キヤノン (Canon)
- ニコン (Nikon)
- ソニー (Sony)

COLLOCATIONS:
- {一眼|いちがん}レフで{撮|と}る (to shoot with an SLR)
- {一眼|いちがん}レフ{用|よう}のレンズ (lens for SLR)

RELATED TERMS:
- コンパクトカメラ (compact camera)
- ミラーレス (mirrorless camera)
- {露出|ろしゅつ} (exposure)
